artefact: REVIEW of prefix P-A -- task 1.6 of openspec/changes/design-campaign-authority-and-sync (discard-time flush of pending client mutations)
reviewer: independent reviewer (persistence/authority scope, read-only; not the author)
verdictSummary: Spec conformance on the flush's own contract is exact -- same route, method, headers, body shape, baseVersion source, envelope construction and never-acknowledged semantics as putLiveCampaign; measurement is byte-accurate; the typed skip reason matches the pin; the wiring pair is idempotent, SSR-guarded and uninstalled on teardown; beforeunload is correctly absent; the 14 rows are real, non-tautological and the red logs are genuine. Two BLOCKING defects arise from the hidden-transition trigger, which fires on ordinary tab switches where the document SURVIVES -- a case the spec's scenarios (all phrased around a discard) never cover: (RE-1) the unconditional clearAutoSaveTimer() cancels the armed ordinary save even on the over-cap branch that then issues nothing, opening a data-loss window that did not exist before this change; (RE-2) a surviving document is left dirty with no scheduled save and, if the keepalive write landed, a stale baseVersion that turns the next ordinary save into a self-caused 409 whose only offered resolution discards post-return edits.

checks.clause: legacyUnadopted -> silent no-op; is silence justified per D8?
checks.result: PASS -- silence is JUSTIFIED; recommendation is to KEEP it as-is
checks.recommendation: Keep the silent no-op. Do NOT add a distinct skip reason.
checks.rationale: Three reasons, all code-cited. (1) The adoption gate is already the loudest state in the app: `legacyUnadopted` is rendered as a persistent adoption offer at CampaignSharePanel.tsx:112 (`if (legacyUnadopted)`) and as a per-campaign badge at src/pages/gameplay/campaigns/index.tsx:66 (`{campaign.legacyUnadopted && (`). The condition the user must act on is already on screen; a second, flush-scoped diagnostic would be a duplicate signal for the same fact. (2) The skip is NOT a degraded flush: runSave already returns `{ status: 'skipped' }` for the same copy (:580-582), so no PUT reaches the server on this path today with or without the flush -- nothing was measured and then abandoned, which is the exact distinction the over-cap reason exists to report. (3) The D8 gate is about the server not ACQUIRING an unadopted copy by accident; a flush without this guard would be the FIRST write to make the server hold that record. The guard is therefore load-bearing, not cosmetic -- and the author proved it load-bearing rather than asserting it (see section 4, mutation proof).
checks.note: The guard is a THIRD skip condition the task text did not enumerate (task 1.6 names only not-dirty and co-op). It is correctly disclosed as DN-2 in the author evidence and is accepted here.

checks.clause: at-most-once per pending set; flag cannot suppress a legitimate second flush; not shared across campaigns/instances incorrectly
checks.evidence: `let pendingFlushIssued = false;` at module scope (:220), set at :933, cleared by markDirty at :945 (`// Genuinely new pending work: a later discard may flush again.`) and by reset at :1027. Row test:207-215 proves a new markDirty re-enables the flush (2 requests); row test:198-205 proves repeated calls on the SAME pending set produce 1.
checks.moduleVsStoreScope: The flag is module-level while the store is a module-level zustand singleton (:1033), so the scopes coincide -- there is no per-instance divergence to get wrong. Cross-campaign leakage was checked and does not occur: runLoad sets `dirty: false` and `baseVersion: migrated.version` on load (:763-766), and the flush's first guard is `!state.dirty`, so a stale true flag from campaign A cannot suppress anything for campaign B before B is mutated -- and the first mutation of B clears it.
checks.onlyResidual: A second discard with NO intervening mutation is suppressed. This is stricter than the spec's 'at most one such write SHALL be issued per discard' and is harmless (the body would be byte-identical). Accepted.

section3_headValidationAnd409.verdict: "never loses an acknowledged revision" IS preserved. No write is duplicated or reordered at the server. But a NEW client-side loss path is introduced on the surviving-document trigger.
section3_headValidationAnd409.serverTrace: src/services/campaignPersistence/CampaignPersistenceService.ts:126-128 -- `if (baseVersion !== currentVersion) { return conflictFromStoredRow(row, prepared.record, hostInstanceId); }`; on match it writes `nextVersion = baseVersion + 1` inside `db.transaction`. The CAS is a strict equality on the campaigns-table write counter and the write is transactional, so two PUTs carrying the same baseVersion cannot both commit: exactly one wins, the other 409s. No duplication, no reordering, and a flush that loses the CAS cannot overwrite the acknowledged revision that won it -- the spec scenario 'An unread flush never claims a revision it did not earn' holds as written.
clientTraceAfterAnAcceptedKeepalivePut: The flush does not advance baseVersion (pinned by test:297-299) and does not clear dirty.

The armed debounce was cleared at :908, and NOTHING re-arms it: the only re-arm site is markDirty:955, and the only baseVersion resync sites are runLoad:766 and resolveConflictTakeServer:985. There is no visible-transition or focus reconciliation anywhere in src/ (verified by grep: campaignPersistenceWiring.ts is the only campaign-path visibilitychange listener).
So the next ordinary save reads the OLD baseVersion at runSave:632 and 409s against the server's incremented counter.

runSave takes the single-attempt branch (:653-657): `set({ saveState: 'conflict', conflictServerRecord, saveConflict })`. Auto-save then self-disables -- the debounce callback early-returns while saveState === 'conflict' (:957-959).

The only resolution offered is take-server: CampaignSaveStatusCard.tsx:171 `data-testid="campaign-conflict-take-server-btn"` -> resolveConflictTakeServer:976-991 calls writeLiveCampaign(serverCampaign) and sets dirty:false. There is no keep-local path.
section3_headValidationAnd409.acknowledgedRevisionSafety: PRESERVED. Nothing here can lose a revision the server acknowledged -- the loss is of UN-acknowledged local work made after the tab returned, discarded by the only conflict resolution the UI offers.
section3_headValidationAnd409.duplicationOrReordering: NONE at the server (transactional CAS). Client-side, the flush is not sequenced through `saveChain` (:597-607) or awaited against `inFlightLoad` (:615-618), so it can race an in-flight ordinary save; the CAS still admits exactly one, and the loser surfaces as a 409 conflict card rather than a silent overwrite. Acceptable, but it belongs in the receipt.

requiredEdits.title: The over-cap branch cancels the armed ordinary save and then issues nothing -- a data-loss window this change INTRODUCES
requiredEdits.finding: useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:907-908 runs `clearAutoSaveTimer()` unconditionally, BEFORE the body is built and before the cap test at :919. On the over-cap branch (:919-932) the action then sets flushSkip and returns having fired nothing. The armed ordinary save it just killed has NO 64 KiB cap -- putLiveCampaign (:517-525) is a plain fetch with no keepalive flag -- so the debounced save that was about to succeed is destroyed and replaced with nothing. Sequence: mutate at t=0 (timer armed for t=2s); tab switch at t=1s -> visibilitychange hidden -> over-cap skip -> timer cleared, no request; user never mutates again and later closes. Pre-change that mutation was saved at t=2s. Post-change it is lost. Strictly worse than the baseline, and it fires precisely for the large campaigns the task says are the growth risk.
requiredEdits.contrastWithinTheSameChange: The legacyUnadopted guard returns at :893, BEFORE :908, so it correctly leaves the armed timer intact -- and the author pinned that in test:255-259 (`// Still dirty, and the armed timer is left alone`). The same reasoning was not applied to the over-cap branch.
requiredEdits.specPosition: Moving the clear is spec-conformant. The `AND the armed debounce timer SHALL be cleared, so the discard path and the timer cannot both write` bullet lives in the scenario where a write IS issued (spec.md, 'A mutation inside the debounce window survives a hard reload'). The over-cap scenario requires only that no request be issued and a typed diagnostic be recorded; it says nothing about the timer, and clearing it there serves no invariant because there is no second writer to collide with.
requiredEdits.exactEdit: In flushPendingMutationsAction: DELETE the `clearAutoSaveTimer();` call and its comment at useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts:907-908, and INSERT `clearAutoSaveTimer();` immediately before `pendingFlushIssued = true;` at :933 (i.e. on the branch that actually fires, still before fireKeepaliveFlush, preserving 'the discard path and the armed timer cannot both write').
requiredEdits.requiredTestRow: Add to the store-action describe block: an over-cap campaign flushes, asserts 0 captured requests and flushSkip.reason === 'envelope-over-keepalive-cap' (as today), then advances AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS and settles promises, and asserts exactly ONE captured request whose init.keepalive is undefined -- i.e. the ordinary uncapped PUT still ran. Red-first against the current code (it captures 0).

requiredEdits.title: A hidden transition the document SURVIVES leaves the client dirty with nothing scheduled and a stale baseVersion -- a self-caused 409 whose only resolution discards post-return edits
requiredEdits.finding: visibilitychange->hidden fires on every ordinary tab switch, minimise and app switch; the document is NOT discarded. The implementation treats that case identically to a discard. After it fires: (a) the armed debounce is gone (:908) and nothing re-arms it -- the only re-arm site is markDirty:955 -- so `dirty` stays true with NO scheduled save, which renders a permanent 'Unsaved changes' badge at CampaignSaveStatusCard.tsx:111-113; (b) if the keepalive write landed, the server counter is now baseVersion+1 (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:129-134) while the client still holds the old value (pinned by test:297-299), so the user's NEXT mutation debounces into runSave:632 with a stale baseVersion, the CAS at :126-128 refuses it, and runSave:653-657 sets saveState 'conflict' -- after which auto-save self-disables (:957-959); (c) the only resolution the UI offers is take-server (CampaignSaveStatusCard.tsx:171 -> resolveConflictTakeServer:976-991), which overwrites the live campaign with the server record and sets dirty:false, DISCARDING every edit made after the tab returned. There is no keep-local path. Verified by grep: no visible-transition, focus or head re-validation exists anywhere in the campaign path to resync baseVersion.
requiredEdits.whyNotCoveredBySpecToday: All four scenarios of the requirement are phrased around `the document is discarded or becomes hidden` with the discard as the model case; none describes the state the client is left in when the document survives the hidden transition. This is a genuine gap in the delta, not merely an implementation slip -- which is why the fix needs a spec scenario, not just code.
requiredEdits.exactEdit: Preferred (keeps the pinned 'cannot both write' invariant intact, because the timer is only re-armed on a document PROVEN to have survived): (1) In useCampaignPersistenceStore.ts add an action `reconcileAfterDiscardFlush: () => void` that, when `pendingFlushIssued && get().dirty && !isCoopCampaign(readLiveCampaign()) && !get().legacyUnadopted && get().saveState !== 'conflict'`, re-arms the same debounce markDirty arms (:955-961) -- the document survived, so an acknowledged save is still owed and the flush was never an acknowledgement. (2) In campaignPersistenceWiring.ts handleVisibilityChange (:52-56) add the else branch: on `document.visibilityState === 'visible'`, call `useCampaignPersistenceStore.getState().reconcileAfterDiscardFlush()`. (3) Add ONE spec scenario under the same requirement, e.g. '#### Scenario: A hidden transition the document survives still reaches an acknowledged save' -- GIVEN a flush was issued on a hidden transition and the document was not discarded / WHEN the document becomes visible again / THEN the client SHALL schedule an ordinary acknowledged save, because an unread flush is not an acknowledgement and the client SHALL NOT be left dirty with no pending write. (4) Test rows: hidden-then-visible re-arms and the ordinary (non-keepalive) PUT fires on advancing AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS; and hidden-then-visible-then-mutate does not double-arm.
requiredEdits.acceptableAlternative: If the parent judges the reconciliation out of prefix scope, the alternative is to PIN the accepted consequence rather than leave it undocumented: add the spec scenario stating that a surviving hidden transition may leave the client dirty until the next mutation and that the resulting 409 is expected, AND add a test row that pins the stale-baseVersion 409 so the behaviour is owned rather than discovered later. What is NOT acceptable is shipping the trigger with neither the fix nor the pin -- the 'Unsaved changes' badge with nothing scheduled, and the take-server-only conflict, are user-visible and lossy.
requiredEdits.notAnOption: Dropping the hidden trigger. Task 1.6 mandates it, and mobile browsers deliver hidden where they never deliver pagehide.

nonBlockingObservations.note: flushSkip has ZERO consumers -- grep over src/ finds it only in the store and the new test. The spec says 'record a typed skip diagnostic' and the task says 'record a TYPED diagnostic on the store', so this is conformant as written, and there is in-repo precedent for the shape (task 1.5's receipt closes with the same honest NON-CLAIM about the campaign-list omissions header having no UI consumer yet). Worth carrying forward as an explicit NON-CLAIM in the 1.6 receipt: the condition is recorded but nothing yet shows it to anyone.

The flush is not sequenced through saveChain (:597-607) and does not await inFlightLoad (:615-618), unlike runSave. Both races are refused safely by the server CAS and neither can produce a silent overwrite, but the asymmetry with the ordinary save path should be named in the receipt.

__resetCampaignPersistenceCoordinationForTests (:249-252) does not clear pendingFlushIssued; the tests get away with it because they also call reset() (test:159, 332), which does (:1027). Harmless today; a future suite that calls only the coordination reset would inherit a stale flag. One line, at the author's discretion.

doubleFireCheck.proof: armAutoSaveTimer opens with clearAutoSaveTimer() (:890) and autoSaveTimer is a single module-level variable (:227 region, cleared at :264-269), so N visible transitions leave at most ONE pending timeout -- each call replaces the previous rather than stacking. The reconcile itself issues no request, which the pre-existing row "does not flush when the document becomes visible" still proves (0 captures without advancing timers). The gate is also self-terminating: once the re-armed save succeeds, applySavedRecord sets dirty:false (:555) and every later visible transition short-circuits on `!state.dirty`.

inFlightSaveCheck.question: can it re-arm during an in-flight save, and does that race or reorder anything?
inFlightSaveCheck.answer: It CAN re-arm while saveState is 'saving' -- and that is safe. No race, no reorder, no lost write.
inFlightSaveCheck.proof: performSave serializes every write through saveChain (:604-614, comment: "Serializing is what makes `baseVersion` a usable compare-and-swap token"), so a reconcile-armed save is queued BEHIND the in-flight one and runSave reads get().baseVersion (:640 region) only after the earlier save applied its record. The server CAS (CampaignPersistenceService.ts:126-128) is the backstop either way.
inFlightSaveCheck.residualShapeIsPreExisting: The one observable side effect is a possible redundant PUT of unchanged state: applySavedRecord does NOT clear the timer (:546-562 -- no clearAutoSaveTimer among the seven call sites at :587, :847, :890, :959, :1017, :1085), and runSave does not gate on dirty, so a timer armed before a concurrently-completing save still fires. That shape ALREADY exists on the markDirty path (markDirty arms a timer that survives a save completing underneath it) and predates this prefix -- the reconcile inherits it rather than introducing it. Version churn only; no data loss, no reordering. Not a required edit.
inFlightSaveCheck.conflictExclusionIsCorrect: Excluding saveState === 'conflict' is right, not a gap: the debounce callback already early-returns on conflict (:893-895), so re-arming there would arm a timer that can only no-op, and auto-save is deliberately disabled until the player resolves.

re2.bfcacheBonus: Unintended but welcome: a document that fires pagehide, enters bfcache and is later restored also becomes visible again, so the reconciliation re-arms the owed save on bfcache restore -- the exact case the deliberate absence of beforeunload was protecting.
testRows: "re-arms the ordinary save when a document the flush assumed lost becomes visible again" -- hidden gives 1 keepalive request; visible + advancing the debounce gives a SECOND request with `keepalive` undefined. Non-tautological: without the reconcile the flush had cleared the timer, so advancing produces nothing.

"reaches the existing conflict flow when the flush landed and the re-armed save is stale" -- re-stubs fetch to the typed 409 a landed keepalive write causes, then asserts saveState 'conflict', saveConflict.reason 'base-state-unavailable', recoveryAction 'resync-to-active-head', conflictServerRecord.version === BASE_VERSION + 1 and dirty still true. Pins the residual rather than papering over it; invents no UI and adds no resolution path.

residualAssessment.residualAsStatedByAuthor: The reconciliation re-arms a SAVE; it does not re-validate the cache against the stream head and does not resync baseVersion. A landed keepalive write therefore still routes the next save into the existing 409 conflict flow, whose only resolution remains take-server.
residualAssessment.howPinned: Three surfaces, not one: (1) a passing test row that drives the exact 409 and asserts the resulting store state; (2) an explicit entry in correction2.nonClaimsAddedOnReviewerRequest naming what eliminating it would require ("head re-validation on return, which is not in this prefix and not in task 1.6"); (3) the spec scenario says only that an acknowledged save SHALL be SCHEDULED -- it does not claim the conflict is avoided, so the spec and the code agree.
why: Scope: task 1.6 NON-CLAIMS already exclude head machinery ("no change to the PUT route or its CAS"), and the task text itself defers re-validation to task 1.3 ("the next load re-validates the cache against the head per task 1.3"). Adding head re-validation here would be scope growth into another task.

Harm is materially reduced, not merely relabelled. Before commit D the 409 was the DEFAULT outcome and arrived arbitrarily late -- whenever the user next mutated, after arbitrarily much new work, with take-server discarding all of it. After commit D the reconcile save fires ~AUTO_SAVE_DEBOUNCE_MS after the tab returns, at which point local content is still identical to the flushed body, so take-server adopts an equivalent record and resyncs baseVersion losslessly. The lossy case narrows to the race where the user edits within the debounce window of returning.

It is now owned in state, not hidden: the conflict carries the server's typed reason and record through the flow the store already models, and the client never claims an acknowledgement it did not earn -- the invariant the requirement actually asserts.
residualAssessment.followUpRecommendation: NON-BLOCKING, and a PARENT action rather than an author edit: when the parent flips the 1.6 checkbox, carry this residual (and NB-1, the unconsumed flushSkip) into the task receipt in tasks.md, so it lives on an SSOT surface instead of only in the planning evidence JSON. Head re-validation on return-to-visible is the natural task 1.3 follow-up.
